topicDefinitions.boundary: Input acceptance and rejection at a local crossing
topicDefinitions.determinism: Repeated processing under fixed effective inputs and a stated equality of outcomes
topicDefinitions.projection: Keeping required meaning/referents during a changed representation, with named intentional losses
topicDefinitions.persistence: Publishing or reconstructing stored state, with error/recovery and staging/cache authority distinctions

judgmentMeaning.negative: Local responsibility does not apply, not merely a defective implementation

limits: Procedural independence only: curator and author/reviewers use the same model family and share the surrounding task framing. This is not independent human judgment or a population sample.

Selection was completed before candidate drafting. No candidate definitions, product plan, adoption mappings/README or reviewer outputs were read. The permitted readiness inventory contained family identifiers and inherited role labels; these were visible but no candidate clause text was used.
Known stress cases are not held out. Fresh subjects are new at the selected symbol scope but come from the same twelve local repositories.
Positive means the local responsibility applies, not that an implementation satisfies it. Source comments are author testimony and no application test outcomes were collected.

Function-level subjects in the same file share implementation/library dependencies and are not statistically independent samples. Read and write entries are separate responsibilities, not separate storage engines.
References freeze expected roles/facets as unknown; no new standardized role/facet judgment is inferred from inherited labels.
Reviewer-facing corpus excludes topic expectations and usefulness answers. Local descriptions still naturally reveal source duties; this is blinded to answers, not anonymized source.
Source files are included as finite excerpts and whole-file digests. Uninspected delegated code remains a limitation even if entry documentation states a contract.
